t: Listen to a talk in an Earth science class.
Ask people why we have seasons, and many will say it's because Earth is closer to the sun in summer.
That's a common idea, but it's wrong.
In fact, Earth is slightly closer to the sun in January, which is winter in the Northern Hemisphere.
The primary reason for the seasons is the tilt of Earth's axis, about twenty-three and a half degrees.
When your hemisphere is tilted toward the sun, sunlight hits the ground more directly and the days are longer, so it's summer.
When it's tilted away, the light is spread out and the days are short.
Distance plays only a very small role.
